title: San Juan Islands, Washington
seoTitle: Charter Bus to the San Juan Islands, Washington
excerpt: A charter bus to the San Juan Islands stops at Anacortes. Why groups walk onto the ferry, where to see whales, and how to plan around the sailing times.

heroImage.alt: Forested islands and calm water in the San Juan archipelago seen from a ferry deck

extraImage.alt: An orca surfacing off the rocky shoreline at Lime Kiln Point on San Juan Island

body.text: The San Juans are an archipelago of a few hundred islands in the strait between Washington and Vancouver Island, four of them served by ferry. They sit in a rain shadow, so they get noticeably better weather than Seattle, and they are one of the best places in the lower 48 to see orcas from land. A charter bus to the San Juan Islands is, in practice, a charter bus to Anacortes — and that is usually the right way to do it.
Walk onto the ferry

Washington State Ferries run to the islands from Anacortes, and vehicle space in summer requires a reservation booked well in advance. Space for a full-size coach is limited and expensive, and for most group visits it is not worth it.

The standard arrangement is a charter to the Anacortes terminal, the group walking on as foot passengers, and island transport at the other end. Walk-on tickets need no vehicle reservation, the crossing to Friday Harbor takes about an hour, and Friday Harbor itself is compact enough to explore on foot.
The coach either waits at Anacortes or returns to collect in the evening. Tell your operator which you want when you ask for a price — the two arrangements produce quite different numbers.
Which island

items: San Juan Island: the most visited, with Friday Harbor as the main town, the Whale Museum, and Lime Kiln Point State Park on the west side. The default choice for a group.
Orcas Island: the largest and most rural, with Moran State Park and the road up Mount Constitution for the best view in the archipelago.
Lopez Island: flat, quiet and the cyclists' island, with far fewer visitors.
Shaw Island: tiny, with almost no visitor facilities. Not a group destination.

body.text: The whales, honestly

Lime Kiln Point on the west side of San Juan Island is known as Whale Watch Park and is one of very few places in the world where orcas are regularly seen from shore. It is a genuine possibility, not a guarantee.

The Southern Resident orcas that made the islands famous have declined and now spend less time in these waters. Transient orcas, humpbacks and minke whales are seen regularly, and boat-based tours have far better odds than standing on a headland. If whales are the reason your group is coming, book a tour rather than relying on the park, and set expectations either way.
Which charter bus fits the mainland leg

items: Forty to fifty-six: a full-size [charter bus](/fleet/charter-buses) for the run from Seattle or Bellingham to Anacortes, with luggage bays for an overnight group.
Twenty to thirty-two: a [mini bus](/fleet/mini-buses) is the practical size if you genuinely want a vehicle on the island, and far cheaper on the ferry.
Ten to fourteen: a [sprinter van](/fleet/sprinter-vans) crosses easily and suits a small corporate retreat.

body.text: Corporate retreats to the islands are a steady part of our shoulder-season work, handled by our [corporate travel](/services/corporate-travel) team, with ferry-timed transfers at both ends.
Getting to the ferry

[Anacortes](/locations/washington/anacortes) is about ninety minutes north of [Seattle](/locations/washington/seattle) and forty minutes from [Bellingham](/locations/washington/bellingham). We also run pickups from [Mount Vernon](/locations/washington/mount-vernon) and [Everett](/locations/washington/everett).

Build in real buffer. Ferries leave on time, summer queues at Anacortes are long, and a group that misses a sailing waits for the next one — which on some routes is two hours. Groups searching for charter bus rental near me for an island trip should give the operator the sailing time rather than a desired arrival time.
What a day on San Juan Island looks like

Friday Harbor is small enough to walk in twenty minutes, so a group arriving on foot has an easy start: the Whale Museum is a few blocks from the dock, and the harbor front carries most of the restaurants and shops on the island.

Getting to Lime Kiln Point on the far side needs transport — it is about ten miles across the island. The island shuttle runs in season, and for a group on a schedule it is worth arranging transport in advance rather than hoping. English Camp and American Camp, the two halves of San Juan Island National Historical Park, commemorate a border standoff in 1859 that began with a shot pig and nearly started a war, which is a better story than most national parks can offer.
A day trip covers Friday Harbor and one other stop comfortably. Seeing the whole island properly, or adding Orcas, needs an overnight.
When to go

June through September is the season: dry, warm by Pacific Northwest standards, and with the best whale watching from late spring into autumn. July and August are the busiest and the hardest for ferry space. From October the islands quiet substantially and many businesses reduce hours, which makes for a peaceful and inexpensive trip if nobody is expecting the summer version.
Booking the trip

Book the ferry first, then send us the sailing times with your headcount and pickup point. [Request an all-in quote](/quote) and you will usually have an itemized price back the same day, driver, fuel, tolls and taxes included.
